content.thinking:
I'm laying out the postmortem facts: the monthly-spend flag was turned on by an admin at 10:07, and from that point spend_summary.py line 47 is throwing a ZeroDivisionError. Argus turned the flag off at 10:13:58, yet the logs still show it as on at 10:15, so I need to check that discrepancy.

I'm checking whether the code-fix reading was ever actually run, and it wasn't, so the claim that the cause rests on it stays unverified. The logs show the error at line 47 continuing past the 10:14 switch-off, which means the flag revert never reached the service.

I'm working through the stop-the-harm step: switch monthly-spend-feature off again and confirm at the service that the evaluation logs read off and the division errors stop, since the last switch-off didn't seem to reach the service. I'm also ruling out recent changes: no deploys came back, all replicas run one revision, and the one-day lookback shows nothing earlier than the flag switch.

I'm confirming the deploy check: one production change came back (the flag itself), and the rollout had converged on a single revision. Pages rendered normally before 10:07, so the failure starts with the flag. Next I'm tracing the causal chain, beginning with shoppers' account pages failing, then the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py line 47 that began in the same minute the service started evaluating the flag.

I'm tracing the causal chain now: the service started taking the monthly spend summary path once an admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at 10:07, and I'm checking which rows show that switch-on. The breakage comes from the code itself, which per the unrun reading divides the month's total by the count of this month's purchases, so shoppers who bought earlier but not this month hit a zero divisor at line 47.

I'm checking the root-cause sentence against the record: the flag turns on the monthly spend path, which divides by this month's purchase count, so shoppers with earlier purchases but none this month hit a zero divisor at line 47.

I'm writing the root-cause sentence: the monthly summary the flag turns on divides by this month's purchase count, which is zero for shoppers who bought earlier but not this month, so the account page fails at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py.

I'm now writing the stop-the-harm step as the account pages are still failing for shoppers while the feature stays on, and a switch-off may not reach the service. I'm keeping the root-cause statement tied to the division at line 47 and the shoppers who bought before but not this month.

I'm now checking the remaining concern: the account pages could keep failing for shoppers the summary path breaks on while the feature is back on, and a switch-off might again fail to reach the service. Next I'm listing the contributing factors, starting with the absence of a test covering accounts with no purchases this month before the flag went to production.

I'm moving on to the contributing factors: the flag went to all traffic at once, with no gradual rollout, and the switch-off never reached the service even though it should have stopped the harm sooner.

I'm weighing the contributing factors now: the flag went to all traffic at once, the switch-off never reached the service, and the page was not routed to a person. I'm checking whether each one held before the incident, since that decides whether it counts as a cause.

I'm listing the action items now, starting with a prevent item: a check before enabling that flag-gated code paths are covered by tests for accounts with no purchases this month.

I'm drafting the action items now: first a prevent item requiring tests on a flag's on path, including accounts with no purchases this month, to pass before the flag can be switched on in production. Next is a rollout item, turning io-shop flags on for a small share of shoppers first and widening only while the account page error rate stays at baseline. I'm also adding a detect item so the service reports which flag version it actually evaluated, making a switch that never arrives visible.

I'm now settling the last two items: a check that turns the flag's on path into a required test before it can go live, and a rollout that starts with a small share of shoppers. The reporting step will show which flag value each replica actually evaluates, so a switch that never arrives becomes visible, and I'll wire the on-call page for the io-shop error rate, which nobody received.

I'm now noting why the switch-off didn't help: the service kept evaluating the flag as on after the provider recorded it off, so I need to find out whether the change reached the service at all, and why the division errors kept going if it did. I'm also recording what went well: the investigator tied the onset to the flag change, and the mitigation agent reverted the flag and then checked the service before deciding the revert hadn't taken effect.

I'm noting what went well in the response: the Investigator Agent timed the onset and tied it to the flag change, and the Mitigation Agent reverted the flag and then checked the service instead of assuming the revert had taken effect.

I'm checking the Mitigation Agent's revert: the flag switch-off never changed what the service evaluated, so calling C1 refuted tested nothing, and putting the flag back on re-enabled the path the logs tie to the errors.

I'm noting that the flag never switched off at the service, which makes the earlier revert untested for C1. I'm also keeping a short list of what the analysis takes as given: the mechanism comes from reading the source rather than running it, and the account page failures are assumed to account for the error rise.

I'm checking the rest of the timeline against the record now: the flag switch-on at {P1.1} sent account pages through the monthly spend summary, and before that the service was healthy with the flag off.

I'm checking the rest of the write-up: the summary path divides by a shopper's purchases this month, which the code reading shows is zero for shoppers who bought earlier but not this month. Next I'm making sure the went-well items name who acted and when.

action_items.item: Require tests that run a feature flag's on path in io-shop, including accounts with no purchases in the current month, to pass before that flag can be switched on in production.
Switch io-shop feature flags on for a small share of shoppers first, and widen them only while the account page error rate stays at its baseline.
Have each io-shop replica report the flag values it evaluates, and alert when they still differ from the flag provider's values after a change should have arrived.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page so that a person takes up incidents Argus escalates.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service logged a rising account page error rate.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors first appeared in the minute the incident began and kept coming in every minute after it.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: the production change events read for the day before the onset came back with only the flag change, and no deploys.
A rollout caught part-way: all replicas ran one revision when the deployment was read.

causal_chain.step: The service started sending account pages through the monthly spend summary when admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. Before that it evaluated the flag off on every request. In that minute it evaluated the flag partly on, and on every request after that.
The summary path divides by the number of a shopper's purchases this month, and Code-Fix's reading of the source finds that number is zero for shoppers who have bought before but not this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: An administrator switched on a new monthly spending summary for shoppers' account pages, and the calculation behind it divides by zero, likely for shoppers who have bought before but not this month, so their account pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: Before the flag was switched on in production, no test or check was seen covering the monthly spend summary path for an account with no purchases this month. Code-Fix's reading says the existing test helper calls that the ordinary case.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been found before any shopper reached the summary path.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: monthly-spend-feature went from off to on for every request at once. The service evaluated it on for all requests from the minute after the switch, and no gradual rollout was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have hit the failing path, and the rollout could have been stopped before most account pages failed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: Switching the flag off at the provider did not change what the service evaluated. The service's logs still show monthly-spend-feature evaluated on after the provider recorded it off.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Argus's switch-off would have taken the service off the failing path and ended the harm soon after it was made.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent formed a single candidate that tied the onset to admin switching monthly-spend-feature on.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature off, a change that can be put back.
The Mitigation Agent looked at the service before judging the revert, rather than assuming it had worked.
The Investigator Agent read the logs again after the revert. They show the service still evaluating the flag on.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #420.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

The Mitigation Agent judged C1 refuted and put monthly-spend-feature back on, even though the service's logs show the flag never went off at the service. That put back a flag the logs tie to the failures.

input.root_cause: The monthly spend summary path that monthly-spend-feature turns on, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, divides the account's total for this month by the number of purchases in the current month. That number is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month, so the function raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: With monthly-spend-feature back on, account pages could keep failing for shoppers the summary path breaks on, and switching the feature off might again fail to reach the service.
input.stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. Then confirm at io-shop that its evaluation log lines read monthly-spend-feature=off, that the ZeroDivisionError account page failures stop, and that the error rate falls back near {errors_before}.
input.why_it_did_not_help: Find out why io-shop still evaluated monthly-spend-feature as on at {Gce95.7}, after the flag provider recorded it switched off at {P2.1}. First establish whether the change reached the service's flag evaluation at all, for example through caching, propagation or a stale client. If it did, find out why the division errors went on.
